issue.body:
We have some [Vulkan Validation Layers](https://github.com/KhronosGroup/Vulkan-ValidationLayers) errors that https://github.com/openxla/iree/pull/15884 uncovered by changing our  reporting from simply logging to also returning failure statuses. Those failure statuses then cause tests to fail if any validation layer errors are present.

Validation layers can also be used in conjunction with "profiles" (discussed here: https://github.com/openxla/iree/issues/15299) to test a range of hardware capabilities on a single device. In order to have a good signal-to-noise ratio, we should first fix existing validation layer errors or at least tag affected tests as needing fixes.

Here are the errors I've seen so far:

## `vkFlushMappedMemoryRanges` must respect `VkPhysicalDeviceLimits::nonCoherentAtomSize`

In these tests (on NVIDIA):
* `iree/hal/drivers/vulkan/cts/vulkan_command_buffer_test`
* `iree/tests/e2e/stablehlo_models/mnist_train_test/mnist_train_test_vulkan`

([full logs here](https://github.com/openxla/iree/actions/runs/7216253462/job/19662333021#step:6:2903))
`[VULKAN] ! Validation Error: [ VUID-VkMappedMemoryRange-size-01390 ] Object 0: handle = 0xe88693000000000c, type = VK_OBJECT_TYPE_DEVICE_MEMORY; | MessageID = 0xdd4e6d8b | vkFlushMappedMemoryRanges: Size in pMemRanges[0] is 0x4, which is not a multiple of VkPhysicalDeviceLimits::nonCoherentAtomSize (0x40) and offset + size (0x0 + 0x4 = 0x4) not equal to the memory size (0x40). The Vulkan spec states: If size is not equal to VK_WHOLE_SIZE, size must either be a multiple of VkPhysicalDeviceLimits::nonCoherentAtomSize, or offset plus size must equal the size of memory (https://vulkan.lunarg.com/doc/view/1.3.250.1/linux/1.3-extensions/vkspec.html#VUID-VkMappedMemoryRange-size-01390)`

This only appears to affect the fill buffer tests, but the compiler _could_ still generate code that uses buffers of these sizes.
* We might be able to just disable validation layers on this test, if we don't expect real applications to be affected

`vkFlushMappedMemoryRanges` must respect `VkPhysicalDeviceLimits::nonCoherentAtomSize`. There is a TODO in the code that hints at this: https://github.com/openxla/iree/blob/416e4b4ea42f86927947be45ae83388cf581a10f/runtime/src/iree/hal/drivers/vulkan/native_buffer.cc#L122-L130

We could also adjust the sizes/offsets in `iree_hal_vulkan_native_buffer_invalidate_range`/`iree_hal_vulkan_native_buffer_flush_range` based on the reported `VkPhysicalDeviceProperties` values, or values pulled from https://vulkan.gpuinfo.org/displaydevicelimit.php?name=nonCoherentAtomSize&platform=all (256 on SwiftShader and D3D12, 128 on AMD, 64 on NVIDIA)

## SPIR-V capabilities without requirements

This test (on NVIDIA):
* `iree/tests/e2e/matmul/e2e_matmul_direct_i8_gpu_large_valhall_vulkan-spirv_vulkan`

([full logs here](https://github.com/openxla/iree/actions/runs/7216253462/job/19662333021#step:6:2056))
`[VULKAN] ! Validation Error: [ VUID-VkShaderModuleCreateInfo-pCode-08740 ] Object 0: handle = 0x1e8ff90, type = VK_OBJECT_TYPE_DEVICE; | MessageID = 0x6e224e9 | vkCreateShaderModule(): The SPIR-V Capability (DotProductKHR) was declared, but none of the requirements were met to use it. The Vulkan spec states: If pname:codeType is ename:VK_SHADER_CODE_TYPE_SPIRV_EXT, and pCode declares any of the capabilities listed in the SPIR-V Environment appendix, one of the corresponding requirements must be satisfied (https://vulkan.lunarg.com/doc/view/1.3.250.1/linux/1.3-extensions/vkspec.html#VUID-VkShaderModuleCreateInfo-pCode-08740)`
Same error for `DotProductKHR`, `DotProductInput4x8BitKHR`, `SPV_KHR_integer_dot_product`.

I'm not totally sure from reading the error and the spec how we should be satisfying the "corresponding requirements"... maybe we need to enable the `VK_KHR_shader_integer_dot_product` extension in here: https://github.com/openxla/iree/blob/6f2c98f4fa482f6172cb5129fd45135592772b9e/runtime/src/iree/hal/drivers/vulkan/vulkan_device.cc#L233-L260

## `vkUpdateDescriptorSets` must respect `VkPhysicalDeviceLimits::minStorageBufferOffsetAlignment`

In these tests (and others), **on SwiftShader**;

* `iree/tests/e2e/stablehlo_ops/check_vulkan-spirv_vulkan_abs.mlir`
* `iree/tests/e2e/stablehlo_ops/check_vulkan-spirv_vulkan_add.mlir`
* `iree/tests/e2e/stablehlo_ops/check_vulkan-spirv_vulkan_batch_norm_inference.mlir`
* `iree/tests/e2e/stablehlo_ops/check_vulkan-spirv_vulkan_broadcast.mlir`
* `iree/tests/e2e/stablehlo_ops/check_vulkan-spirv_vulkan_broadcast_add.mlir`

([full logs here](https://github.com/openxla/iree/actions/runs/7216253462/job/19662332869#step:6:2641))
`[VULKAN] ! Validation Error: [ VUID-VkWriteDescriptorSet-descriptorType-00328 ] Object 0: handle = 0x2a35450, type = VK_OBJECT_TYPE_DEVICE; | MessageID = 0xea08144e | vkUpdateDescriptorSets(): pDescriptorWrites[0].pBufferInfo[0].offset (0x40) must be a multiple of device limit minStorageBufferOffsetAlignment 0x100. The Vulkan spec states: If descriptorType is VK_DESCRIPTOR_TYPE_STORAGE_BUFFER or VK_DESCRIPTOR_TYPE_STORAGE_BUFFER_DYNAMIC, the offset member of each element of pBufferInfo must be a multiple of VkPhysicalDeviceLimits::minStorageBufferOffsetAlignment (https://vulkan.lunarg.com/doc/view/1.3.250.1/linux/1.3-extensions/vkspec.html#VUID-VkWriteDescriptorSet-descriptorType-00328)`

Limits are in https://vulkan.gpuinfo.org/displaydevicelimit.php?name=minStorageBufferOffsetAlignment&platform=all. SwiftShader uses 256, mobile devices use 64, some NVIDIA desktop devices uses 16. I see some rounding code already, but this ignores device limits: https://github.com/openxla/iree/blob/6f2c98f4fa482f6172cb5129fd45135592772b9e/runtime/src/iree/hal/drivers/vulkan/descriptor_set_arena.cc#L47-L48
issue.title: Vulkan validation layer errors in tests / on different devices
